Research and retry subagents (workbench/briefs/BRIEF-tax.md, BRIEF-tax-retry.md), every quote checked by the lead against its saved page.

figures.finding: Pay is taxed by the professional income tax (IPR): 3% on the first CDF 1,944,000 a year, 15% to 21,600,000, 30% to 43,200,000 and 40% above, with the tax capped at 30% of taxable pay; income other than pay is in practice not taxed under IPR.

sources.said: Bracket number Taxable bracket (CDF) Gap (CDF) Rates (%) Tax due as per bracket (CDF) Cumulative tax (CDF) From To 1 0 1,944,000 1,944,000 3 58,320.00 58,320.00 2 1,944,001 21,600,000 19,655,999 15 2,948,399.85 3,006,719.85 3 21,600,001 43,200,000 21,599,999 30 6,479,999.70 9,486,716.55 4 43,200,001 And more 40 - - IPR cannot exceed 30% of the taxable salary.

Moreover, the sums paid to casual employees (employees hired on a day-to-day basis) are subject to IPR, but at a preferential rate of 15%. Incomes other than salaries are not subject, in practice, to IPR.

figures.finding: INSS: the employee pays 5% (pension) and the employer 13% (5% pension, 1.5% occupational risks, 6.5% family benefits), plus employer-only INPP training (1% to 3%) and ONEM 0.2%.

sources.said: 1.5% borne by the employer (branch of occupational risks). 5% borne by the employer (pension branch). 5% borne by the worker (pension branch). 6.5% exclusively borne by the employer (family benefits branch).

figures.finding: The employer withholds IPR under PAYE and pays it by the 15th of the next month.

sources.said: IPR is withheld at source by the employer via the pay-as-you-earn (PAYE)
IPR is paid monthly by the employer by the 15th day of the month followin

figures.finding: Payments for services by foreign individuals bear 14% withholding on the gross; royalties bear 20% on 70% of the amount invoiced.
figures.applies: Treaties (Belgium, South Africa) may exempt services.

sources.said: The rate of WHT on amounts paid as compensation for services provided by foreign individuals/entities is 14%, which is based on the gross amount of sums paid.
The tax authorities consider that the net amount of royalties is calculated by deducting 30% from the royalties invoiced (i.e. the taxable basis will be 70% of the royalties invoiced).

figures.finding: Royalties bear 20% withholding on 70% of the invoiced amount (14% of the gross), for residents and non-residents.

sources.said: The standard rate of WHT on dividends, royalties, interest, and directorship fees is 20%, which is based on the gross amount of sums paid.

figures.finding: VAT is 16% (reduced 8%); a person is liable once annual turnover reaches CDF 80,000,000, but members of the liberal professions are liable whatever their turnover.

sources.said: There are three rates: A standard rate of 16%. A reduced rate of 8% applicable to certain products

qui effectuent de manière indépendante, à titre habituel ou occasionnel, des opérations imposables à la TVA et qui réalise un chiffre d’affaires annuel égal ou supérieur à 80 000 000 de Francs congolais. $ Il sied de préciser que les membres des professions libérales sont assujettis à la TVA sans considération de leur chiffre d’affaires

figures.finding: The individual income tax (IRPP) is assessed on the income of a tax year and declared by 30 April of the year after the income was earned.

value.taxYear: the year in which the income is earned

figures.applies: From the IS-IRPP law (Loi n° 23/053 of 30 November 2023), as the DGI states it in October 2025.

sources.said: L’impôt sur le revenu des personnes physiques est déclaré au plus tard le 30 avril de l’année qui suit celle de la réalisation des revenus.

figures.finding: Under the IS-IRPP law (Loi n° 23/053) a resident's individual income tax (IRPP) is charged on his net global income, the sum of his category incomes (salaries, investment income, gains, business and professional profits), by the same scale: 3% to CDF 1,944,000, 15% to 21,600,000, 30% to 43,200,000 and 40% above, never more than 30% of the base; a non-resident is charged on Congolese-source income.
figures.applies: The IRPP as the DGI presents it in 2025-2026; the IPR entry above is the tax on pay within it.

sources.said: La personne physique résidant en République Démocratique du Congo, quelle que soit sa nationalité et la source de ses revenus ; $ La personne physique non résidente qui recueille des revenus de source congolaise ; … L’impôt sur le revenu des personnes physiques est calculé par application du barème à taux progressifs sur le revenu net global qui est la somme de revenus nets catégoriels. En aucun cas, l’impôt calculé ne peut dépasser 30 % de la base imposable. Ce barème est décliné de la manière ci-après : $ 3% pour la tranche de revenus de 0,00 FC à 1.944.000,00 FC ; $ 15% pour la tranche de revenus de 1.944.001,00 FC à 21.600.000,00 FC ; $ 30% pour la tranche de revenus de 21.600.001,00 FC à 43.200.000,00 FC ; $ 40% pour la tranche de revenus excédant 43.200.000,00 FC.
